finding.claim: Authorization bypass in wipe: requireRole returns a boolean that is discarded, so any user (with any roles, including none) can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Caller-supplied User u and tenant string from the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe request (comment at Admin.java:24).

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point
requireRole only returns u.roles().contains(role); never throws (Javadoc line 13 says 'Does not throw')

finding.guards_checked: Only control on path is requireRole, which has no enforcing effect. Compared with export (Admin.java:31-33), which uses checkRole (lines 18-22) and throws SecurityException; wipe lacks the equivalent throw. High confidence from direct comparison.

verdict.guard_found: The only control on the path is requireRole at Admin.java:26, which returns a boolean (line 14-15) that is discarded as a bare statement, so it has no effect. The throwing variant checkRole (lines 18-22) is not called in wipe; export at lines 31-33 uses it correctly. No other file in the directory (only src/Admin.java exists) enforces authentication or authorization before wipe.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 discards the boolean returned by requireRole (Admin.java:14-15, which never throws), so wipe at Admin.java:27 runs `repo.wipe(tenant)` for any caller User, while export at Admin.java:32 correctly uses checkRole.

finding.claim: Role checks are not scoped to tenant: OWNER in any tenant authorizes wipe/export on any other tenant (IDOR-style cross-tenant access).
finding.source: Caller-supplied tenant path parameter; attacker needs an account holding OWNER in some tenant.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at Admin.java:33 and repo.wipe(tenant) at Admin.java:27.

trace.note: User record has only name and roles; no tenant association
checkRole(u, "OWNER") tests a global role string, not tenant membership
repo.export(tenant) uses the caller-supplied tenant without ownership comparison

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-ownership check in Admin.java. Could be enforced by the omitted HTTP caller or Repo implementation, which are not in the repository. Medium confidence.

verdict.guard_found: Admin.java:32 checkRole(u, "OWNER") is the only control on export. It tests a global role string and never compares against the tenant argument, so it does not scope access to tenant. Admin.java:26 requireRole(u, "OWNER") guards wipe, but its boolean return is discarded (bare statement), so it blocks nothing. No tenant-ownership check exists in src/Admin.java. The Repo implementation and the HTTP caller are not in the repository.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: User has no tenant field (Admin.java:4), checkRole tests a global role (Admin.java:32), and export passes the caller's tenant through (Admin.java:33). Whether cross-tenant access is blocked depends on the unseen Repo implementation or HTTP layer, so the tenant-scoping claim cannot be decided from this code. Separately, Admin.java:26 discards requireRole's boolean, so wipe at Admin.java:27 has no effective authorization check at all, which is a stronger defect than the one the candidate reports and is confirmed from this file alone (subject to the caller supplying an authenticated User).

finding.claim: Cross-tenant data export: export passes its role check, so an OWNER of one tenant can export another tenant's data (same root cause as F2, disclosure sink).
finding.source: Caller-supplied tenant path parameter and a user holding OWNER in some tenant.

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) entry point
checkRole succeeds if any OWNER role is held; this role check works correctly

finding.guards_checked: checkRole is effective. Exposure depends on whether F2 holds (no tenant scoping in the omitted caller or Repo). Medium confidence.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is effective: it throws SecurityException when "OWNER" is absent from u.roles(). It is not tenant-scoped, since User (src/Admin.java:4) carries no tenant and nothing compares `tenant` to the caller's tenants. No tenant-scope check exists at src/Admin.java:31-33. Repo.export (src/Admin.java:8) is an interface, and its implementation is not in the directory.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (src/Admin.java:31 entry, :32 checkRole throws without OWNER, :33 repo.export(tenant) with no tenant check), and the attacker is a tenant OWNER, which is a plausible cross-tenant threat. But whether another tenant's data is actually disclosed depends on the Repo.export implementation, which is not present here, so the finding cannot be confirmed from this code and it remains a dependency on F2.
